title: A Novel Hybrid Approach To Drought Forecasting: Leveraging Feature Engineering And Ensemble Methods
abstract: There is a high need for accurate drought predictions that will play a crucial role to analyze and mitigate the adverse effects of climate change, that will help in ensuring agricultural sustainability and disaster management. Looking for the traditional forecasting methods, they often struggle with very highly complex and nonlinear climate patterns of today's world, earlier there used to be a statistical, normally inclined climate pattern, but due to many hazardous gases in this world and also due to global warming, the climate pattern is very uncertain and very nonlinear. Hence, traditional forecasting methods struggle in computing the climate over a region. Therefore, adoption of advanced computational techniques to explore the application of machine learning with the help of datasets can improve accuracy in predicting droughts. Various ML algorithms that include decision trees, support vector machines, deep learning models and image processing helps analyze effectiveness in predicting variations in temperature, precipitation levels, and severe drought conditions. The dataset in the given paper comprises data from reliable resources, with historical meteorological and environmental parameters. The study mainly focuses on the feature selection and how these have been engineered to calculate new features. It then explains in detailed the hybridization of the new features with the machine learning ensembling classifiers to calculate the drought class labels. The evaluation is done on the basis of accuracy rates, precision score, f1 score and evaluation metrics. The developed Hybrid Drought Forecasting Model shows better results than those reported in previous research. It records better accuracy, precision and f1 scores, proving that our selected set of features and ensemble work is strong. It improves our ability to examine climate trends and sort droughts by their severity.
problem: Traditional forecasting methods struggle with the complex and nonlinear patterns of modern climate data, limiting their accuracy in predicting droughts.
method: This paper proposes a hybrid drought forecasting model that combines new features derived from mathematical equations with a Random Forest ensemble classifier to accurately predict drought severity.
task: The task is to forecast drought severity by combining new, mathematically engineered features with an ensemble machine learning classifier to predict drought class labels.
innovation: This paper proposes a novel hybrid drought forecasting model that combines new, mathematically-engineered features with a Random Forest ensemble classifier to achieve high prediction accuracy.

Our model is a Hybrid Drought Forecasting Model system composed of deterministic mathematical models and the probabilistic learning characteristics of Random Forest Classifier. By incorporating these elements our model utilizes mathematics models for accurate representations of physical or theoretical associations identifying these asso- ciations while leaving the Random Forest Classifier to generate complex, non-linear patterns that are exhibited in the data.

Mean Absolute Error (MAE): MAE represents the average of the absolute differ- ences between the predicted and actual AQI values. A lower MAE indicates that, on average, the predictions are very close to the true AQI levels.

Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): RMSE computes the square root of the average squared difference between the predicted and observed AQI values. It penalizes larger errors more heavily than MAE, making it suitable for detecting models that struggle with extreme AQI cases.

Coefficient of Determination (R2): R2 measures the proportion of variance in the actual AQI values that is explained by the predictive model. A value closer to 1 indicates strong predictive capability, whereas lower values suggest weaker explanatory power.
